title: Where Is TypeScript Used? knowledge check

questions.prompt: What is the role of TypeScript in a development workflow?
options: It replaces the JavaScript runtime in every browser.
It validates all network data automatically.
It removes the need for runtime tests.
It checks types and improves tooling; the application still runs as JavaScript in its selected runtime.
questions.answer_key: It checks types and improves tooling; the application still runs as JavaScript in its selected runtime.
questions.explanation: Type checking is a development-time layer and does not replace runtime verification.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Where Is TypeScript Used?”?
options: A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with frontend applications and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with frontend applications and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Frontend applications”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Where Is TypeScript Used?”?
options: Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check backend services and apis, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume desktop, mobile, tooling, and library development is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
questions.answer_key: Check backend services and apis, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Backend services and APIs”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
